text:
maria (PM): Quick sync — we need to decide Q3 focus: push for minimal VPC control-plane auth (cross-account token relay + audit) OR land a tiny airgap installer (signed artifacts + bootstrap). Both customers and sales are pushing. Thoughts?

sanjay (eng-runtime): VPC auth is the showstopper for latency-sensitive customers. We need a token-forwarding proxy and cross-account IAM mapping. Rough plan: 1 sprint spike to validate flows, then ~2 sprints to implement core.

kelly (eng-platform): Packaging is heavier but unblocks two pilots. Minimal bundle: one bootstrap binary + tarball of signed images + verification step. Full registry mirror is a later Q4 item. I estimate ~4 sprints for a robust packaged flow if we include mirror tooling.

owen (sec): From security perspective the installer + signing is higher risk if we don't do reproducible builds and detached signatures. Also need to define KMS/HSM custody for private keys. Security review will add ~3 weeks after design freeze.

rebecca (sales): Heads up, MediCloud and Seán Corp both told me they will greenlight pilot contracts if we can provide an airgap minimal installer in Q3. Seán explicitly asked for image signing and a short install runbook. :money_with_wings:

alex (solutions): Splitting scope seems viable: small control-plane slice (token relay + audit events) + thin airgap bundle (bootstrap + signed artifacts). Two small squads in parallel could hit both asks. We must define the public API between them.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Parallel OK, but runtime needs clear auth API and audit schema. I'll own a spike this week to produce sequence diagrams and an auth prototype.

kelly (eng-platform): I'll sketch artifact manifest and bootstrap flow. Reuse our existing CI to produce signed blobs where possible. Example manifest draft:
```yaml
artifact: redwood-private-lite-v1.tar.gz
images:
  - registry.redwood/cp:v1.2.0
  - registry.redwood/worker:v3.5.1
signature: sha256:abcd1234efgh5678...
```
(detached signature + sha256 checksum).

alex (solutions): Also need upgrade semantics and rollback guidance in the pilot checklist. DNS and cert rollover steps must be explicit.

deploy-bot: CI: packaging pipeline currently reporting signature verification failures (12 failures). See https://ci.internal/packaging/987 for logs.

owen (sec): I'll start a short threat model for the installer focused on supply chain tampering and privilege escalation; will propose mitigations (signature verification, least-priv privilege for installer, attestation).

maria (PM): Proposed roadmap ordering to unblock customers quickly:
1) Minimal VPC control-plane auth (token relay + audit) — critical for latency customers
2) Minimal airgap bundle (signed images + bootstrap installer + runbook) — unlock pilots
3) Full packaging (registry mirror, sync tooling, GUI installer) — target Q4
4) KMS/HSM integration + formal compliance artifacts — post-Q4
Agree to this order? If yes I'll update the roadmap PR and add concrete launch criteria.

rebecca (sales): Agree, that order lets us get pilot revenue while we finish the bigger packaging work. I'll coordinate timelines with customers and flag any contractual SLAs.

kelly (eng-platform): I'll drop a WIP spec in #eng-platform by EOD with artifact format and installer steps, and link CI investigations.

sanjay (eng-runtime): 👍 Spike notes will be in runtime/privates-auth repo and I'll link them here once ready.

owen (sec): I'll schedule review sessions for the threat model and bring in infra/sec architects.

alex (solutions): I'll assemble a pilot runbook draft (networking checklist, certs, support on-call rotation) and share with rebecca for customer ops planning.

maria (PM): Action items captured. I'll open the roadmap PR with the prioritized list and tag owners. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
